subject: Sculpting annual commitment: credit tiers, ramp and billing cadence
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acme-retail.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Annual commitment & billing cadence question

Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team is reviewing the numbers and we have two primary concerns before moving to legal: how committed spend maps to monthly billing, and how credits are consumed when our traffic is seasonal (we expect a big spike in Q1). Specifically:

- Can committed credits be sculpted across the year (i.e., larger buckets in certain months) or do they amortize evenly?
- What happens to unused committed credit at year-end when we move to a renewed multi-year commitment?
- What discount bands apply if we commit to a 2-year vs 3-year profile (we have a runway to increase usage each year).

Procurement asked for a simple schedule and an example invoice cadence to show to finance — attaching our traffic plan for context.

Appreciate your help,

Jamie Liu
Head of AI Integrations
Acme Retail

Attachment: Acme_traffic_plan.pdf (1 page summary)
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Annual commitment & billing cadence question

Jamie — thanks for the traffic file, that helps a lot. I pulled together three practical structures for how we can handle committed dollars and billing so you have concrete options to run by finance: see attached Draft_Schedule_v1.xlsx.

Option A — Even Amortization (simple)
- Annual prepay (one invoice), credits placed in a shared "usage credit pool" and consumed as calls occur; monthly billing is only for overages.
- Best for predictable, even usage.

Option B — Sculpted Tiers (recommended for Acme)
- Prepay is allocated to quarterly buckets based on an agreed ramp (Q1 heavier to cover holiday promotions).
- Each bucket has a local burn target; credits move forward but do NOT auto-backfill backwards (we avoid retroactive credits).
- Discounts increase with committed size and multi-year term: 15% (1yr), 22% (2yr), 28% (3yr) — preliminary and negotiable.

Option C — Rolling Wallet with Seasonal Top-ups
- Start with a base prepay pool; we schedule smaller top-up invoices at known seasonal peaks (e.g., Jan).
- Credits in the wallet expire at each anniversary unless replaced by a renew/rollover clause.

Key notes:
- Overages: charged at a pre-agreed incremental rate. We can cap per-month overage exposure.
- True-ups: we offer a Q1/Q4 true-up window to reallocate unused committed credits across buckets for the following year (subject to term).
- Legal / accounting: we provide example invoice templates for finance and a simple SOW redline that captures the rollovers and expiration behavior.

If you like, I can produce a sample 12-month invoice cadence for Option B showing the discount math and expected cashflow.

Thanks — looping in Karthik and Lauren on discounts and contract language.

— Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Rafael — good options. A few commercial clarifications for the Acme team to avoid procurement friction:

1) Discount bands: can we make bands explicit in the quote (i.e., list committed $ thresholds and the effective %, including multi-year stacking)? Procurement likes deterministic tables.
2) Expiration/rollover: recommend a conservative rollover allowance (one quarter) for year-end residuals when they do a renew, otherwise mark residuals as forfeited — finance prefers clarity.
3) Overages cap: propose a soft cap at 20% of monthly bucket; above that we auto-alert the customer and put them on a path to a Top-up PO.

I'll draft the simple clause language and add to SOW redlines. Happy to be on the call with Jamie if procurement wants to walk through the amortization example.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Jamie — appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. Attached is Draft_Schedule_v2.xlsx with a worked example for the two-year trajectory you described (Year 1: +30% Q1 peak; Year 2: +25% growth). High-level summary below: 

- Proposal: Sculpted Tier (Option B) with limited carryover
  - Year 1 prepay: $1.5M (credits placed into Q-level buckets: Jan 40%, Apr 20%, Jul 20%, Oct 20%)
  - Year 2 prepay: $1.875M (25% growth) with a 10% max carryover of unused Year 1 credits into Year 2 unless customer upgrades to a 2-yr firm term, in which case carryover increases to 25% and discount moves to 22%.
  - Expiry: credits not carried into Year 2 are forfeited at renewal unless otherwise agreed in a signed amendment.

- Discount math: we list the effective blended discount in the schedule (22% for 2-yr firm term; 27% for 3-yr firm term). Final percentages subject to legal approval.

- Billing cadence and invoices:
  - Initial prepay invoice due on signature for Year 1.
  - Optional scheduled top-up invoice for Q1 (to fund Jan-heavy month).
  - Overages billed monthly with a 30-day net payment term; overage notifications are automated and routed to procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) We send the v2 schedule to your finance team and procurement for confirmation of carryover language.
2) If they approve, legal will incorporate the carryover clause and we'll send a DocuSign link for signature.
3) We can set up a 30-minute handshake call w/ procurement + revenue ops next Tue (Nov 18) to finalize cadence.

I've also uploaded an invoice cadence example and a redline-friendly clause to the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1789/ACME-2025-ENT-3

Let me know if you want us to widen the carryover band in exchange for a higher committed minimum. Happy to adjust.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Rafael Mendes
